thought.text: The development DB has `pg_trgm` in the `public` schema (which is why it loaded). The production DB has it only in `shared_extensions`, so the `gin_trgm_ops` GIN index in schema.rb can't resolve. Let me add the extensions to `public` in the production DB as well:

reasoning_content:
The reason the development DB worked is that the `pg_trgm` extension exists in the `public` schema (created when the `pg` gem / Rails created it, or by a previous `CREATE EXTENSION` that ran in the search path context). In the production DB, the guide instructs creating the extension in the `shared_extensions` schema, but the schema.rb file creates a GIN index using `gin_trgm_ops`, which requires pg_trgm to be visible in the search_path.

In fact, the guide says to create the extension in `shared_extensions`. But `db/schema.rb` uses `gin_trgm_ops`, which needs the operator class to be resolvable. In the development DB, the extension exists in `public`, so it works.

The cleanest approach: in the production DB, also create pg_trgm (and unaccent) in the `public` schema so that the schema loads. The guide says to place them in `shared_extensions`, but the authoritative schema.rb (which the guide itself also references) needs to be able to resolve `gin_trgm_ops`. Since the development DB had it in `public` and loaded successfully, for the production DB we should do the same thing to make the schema loadable.

Let's add the extension to the public schema of the production DB.

action.command: export PGPASSWORD=root; psql -h localhost -U root -d consul_production -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent;" 2>&1; echo "---"; psql -h localhost -U root -d consul_production -t -c "select e.extname, n.nspname from pg_extension e join pg_namespace n on n.oid=e.extnamespace order by e.extname;"

summary: Add pg_trgm/unaccent to public schema in prod
